raw_tail:
1 first step:** Run `netstat -ano | findstr :8080` to identify the PID holding the port, inspect it with `tasklist`, terminate it with `taskkill /PID <pid> /F`, and restart the server with `npm run dev`.

**Reply 2 first step:** Run `netstat -ano | findstr :8080` in PowerShell, identify the PID with `Get-Process -Id <PID>`, and kill the process with `Stop-Process -Id <PID> -Force`.

If this were my problem, I would act on **Reply 1** first. When dealing with a blocked server throwing `EADDRINUSE`, the immediate priority is finding and killing the orphaned process holding the port so development can resume. Reply 1 places this actionable diagnostic and recovery sequence at the very beginning of the response before explaining that Node 24 is not the cause and detailing long-term prevention (graceful shutdown and nodemon delay). In contrast, Reply 2 buries the necessary first step underneath four paragraphs of conceptual exposition and speculation.
